outline.course: Introductory Statistics (STAT 101 / first-year undergraduate, general-education or social-science track)
outline.audience: First-year undergraduate university students; high-school algebra; no calculus
learningOutcomes: Compute and interpret sample mean, median, and standard deviation in context for a small quantitative dataset.
Distinguish a population parameter from a sample statistic and explain why a statistic can change from sample to sample.
Use a simple repeated-sampling activity to describe the center and spread of sample means qualitatively (no formal CLT).
Identify and correct the misuse of treating one sample mean as if it were the certain population mean.

sections.title: Hook: one number, many stories
sections.purpose: Activate prior ideas about averages and surface uncertainty about generalizing from one sample.

sections.title: Mini-lesson: mean, median, SD in context
sections.purpose: Build shared language for mean, median, and SD as sample summaries in context.

sections.title: Parameter vs statistic
sections.purpose: Separate population targets from sample calculations so later inference talk has a place to land.

sections.title: Activity: many samples, many means
sections.purpose: Make sampling variability visible by comparing many sample means from the same population.

sections.title: Discussion: the overconfident headline
sections.purpose: Practice responsible communication that does not overclaim from one sample mean.

sections.title: Individual check for understanding
sections.purpose: Collect individual formative evidence of the lesson outcomes.
